HasScene.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no scene/rendering layer
HasScene.rationale: TheKinBoss.HasScene => true selects a bespoke Godot combat scene; the sim never renders combat at all.

HasCustomBackground.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no background/rendering layer
HasCustomBackground.rationale: TheKinBoss.HasCustomBackground => true is a pure presentation switch (CreateBackgroundAssetsForCustom vs the act's generic background); the sim has no background/asset concept at all.

CustomBgm.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no audio layer
CustomBgm.rationale: TheKinBoss.CustomBgm names an FMOD event path; the sim has no audio layer at all.

BossNodePath.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no map-node rendering
BossNodePath.rationale: BossNodePath is a map-node icon asset path; the sim's map layer (actmap.py) has no node-rendering concept, only structural point/edge data.

BossNodeSpineResource.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no map-node rendering
BossNodeSpineResource.rationale: Same rationale as BossNodePath -- purely a Spine skeleton resource lookup for map-node rendering.

Slots.maps_to: sts2_rl/monsters/base.py:Encounter.slots (default empty tuple) -- the_kin.py's THE_KIN_BOSS = TheKinEncounter(id="the_kin_boss") passes no slots= kwarg
Slots.issue: TheKinBoss.Slots = ["slot1", "slot2", "leaderSlot"]. The sim's TheKinEncounter dataclass never sets Encounter.slots, and its create_monsters override builds the 3 monsters as a plain list with no slot_name assignment at all. Executed witness: py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py kin-phrog-slots shows `encounter.slots=()` and `slot_name=None` on all 3 creatures. Filed under the shared mechanism encounter/_slot_row_unpopulated (also phrog_parasite/Slots). DORMANT: grepped every C# `SlotName ==` consumer across src/ (Exoskeleton, Myte, PhantasmalGardener, Wriggler) and read KinFollower.cs and KinPriest.cs in full -- neither Kin monster ever reads Creature.SlotName. KinPriest.AfterDeath's 'all followers dead' check (the one behaviourally-live consumer of Kin creature relationships) uses CombatState.GetTeammatesOf (side-based), not slot names. The one place slot order COULD matter mechanically -- CombatManager.AddCreature's SortEnemiesBySlotName resort, ported as the slot_name branch of CreatureCmd.add in sts2_rl/cmds.py -- is never triggered for this unit's own construction (CreatureCmd.add/its sim equivalent is not even in the initial-roster path; TheKinEncounter.create_monsters builds enemies directly) and the 3 monsters' insertion order already matches the intended slot1/slot2/leaderSlot order by construction. The sim's Encounter dataclass CAN express a slot row (Fabricator/Ovicopter use it), so this is a per-unit omission, not a structural limitation.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: none -- the sim has no per-encounter monster-preview member

GetCameraScaling.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no camera/rendering layer
GetCameraScaling.rationale: TheKinBoss.GetCameraScaling => 0.85f is a pure presentation value; the sim never renders combat.

GetCameraOffset.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no camera/rendering layer
GetCameraOffset.rationale: TheKinBoss.GetCameraOffset => Vector2.Down * 50f is a pure presentation value; same rationale as GetCameraScaling.

GenerateMonsters.note: C# GenerateMonsters is a fixed 3-element list: a KinFollower with StartsWithDance mutated True at slot1, a plain KinFollower at slot2, a KinPriest at leaderSlot -- zero base.Rng draws. The sim builds the identical 3-monster roster in the identical order with the dance flag on the first KinFollower only, and 0 draws (create_monsters ignores selection_rng entirely, correctly, since there is nothing to draw). Roster, order, per-instance flag and draw count all match; the dropped slot-name half of each tuple is verdicted separately under Slots above.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: structural: Encounter is never registered with HookSystem

MinGoldReward.note: No override in C#; base ladder for RoomType.Boss is 100. Poverty multiplier out of scope, not applied in roll_gold_reward.
